epic.intent:
## Outcome
A person can call up a **Cult**: one lead agent, the **Magos**, that they talk to in an ordinary terminal chat, plus as many lower-tier **Acolyte** agents as the Magos summons. A cult can be a test swarm on a repository or something playful, such as continuously drawing a plant named Gerry as it grows. The person can start, pause, resume and stop a cult at will. Every run has a time limit. When the limit runs out, the Magos shuts the cult down gracefully and then ends itself.

The design follows Anthropic's Claude Code *agent teams* (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams):

| Agent teams | Cults |
| --- | --- |
| team lead | Magos |
| teammates | Acolytes |
| per-member mailbox | the Skitarii mailbox |
| lead picks teammate models | the Magos picks each acolyte's model, cheapest first |
| shutdown request that a teammate approves | the cult's shutdown protocol |

It departs from agent teams in three places:
- The app, not the agent, enforces the time limit, the acolyte cap, pause and the hard backstop.
- A person can watch acolytes but cannot type to them.
- Each cult has a Shrine that shows what the cult makes.

## User journeys
1. **Found a cult.** In the sidebar's new CULTS section, below AGENTS, press `+`. Enter a name and a charter (what the cult is for). Choose a tracked folder, or none for a project-less cult. Give the Magos a name (a themed name is suggested) and choose its model from the models OMP is signed in to. Set a time limit typed as a duration (`30m` by default, or `90hr`, `2d`, `1d 6h`), or tick **Unlimited**. Set an acolyte cap (default 6). Under Advanced timings, optionally change the shutdown timings. The cult is saved and can be started again later.
2. **Start and talk.** Start creates a new run. A Skitarii (OMP) terminal chat opens for the Magos with the charter and the cult rules, and the person chats with it like any agent.
3. **Acolytes.** The Magos summons acolytes, each a separate OMP chat with a unique **name** (the Magos names it, or the app generates a themed name), a mission and a model. Every cultist is shown by name everywhere: sidebar, terminal headers, the pipeline, the Cult page. By default an acolyte gets the cheapest model OMP is signed in to. The Magos may pick a higher tier, but only with a reason, which the acolyte's row shows. Acolytes appear under the cult's run in the sidebar, following the pattern of the expandable agent rows from DM-619. Their terminals are **watch-only**.
4. **Petitions.** The Magos must ask the person through a **petition** for three things:
   - more acolytes than the cap;
   - **Allow save** (saving plans);
   - orchestrator access to **another tracked folder**.

   Each petition waits on the Cult page with its reason, and the person approves or denies it. An approved petition takes effect on the running Magos without a restart and is revoked when the run ends. A petition still unanswered when the run ends counts as denied. The person can also raise the cap at any time.
5. **Pipeline.** The Cult page shows the cult's pipeline: every message between cultists and every run event (summons, petitions, pause, shutdown, Shrine), by name, live, as read-only plain text.
6. **Pause and resume.** Pause interrupts every member's current turn, stops all wake-ups and freezes the timer. Resume continues.
7. **Stop and expiry.** Stop, or the time running out, starts the graceful shutdown: the Magos orders the acolytes to conclude, they report and exit within the grace window (default 3 m), the Magos writes the run's chronicle (a summary) within its window (default 2 m) and exits, and the app force-ends anything still alive at the hard backstop (grace + window + 1 m). **Kill now** ends everything immediately.
8. **Shrine.** A cult can publish an image (PNG, JPEG or SVG) or an HTML page from its working directory. The Cult page shows the latest one, sandboxed, and updates it live. This is how Gerry is seen growing.

## Confirmed decisions (by the person)
- A cult is a reusable definition with runs. Past runs keep their chronicles.
- Where a cult works is chosen per cult: a tracked folder, or a project-less app-owned directory.
- Pause is soft: it interrupts turns, holds wake-ups and freezes the timer. Processes and context survive.
- The timer counts only running time, not paused time. Expiry runs the graceful shutdown, the hard backstop then force-ends what is left, and quitting the app marks a running run `interrupted`. The default limit is 30 minutes. A limit is typed as any duration of at least 1 minute (`1m`, `90hr`, `2d`), with no upper bound, or set to **Unlimited**, in which case only Stop or Kill now ends the run.
- Shutdown timings: acolyte grace 3 minutes, Magos window 2 minutes, backstop = grace + window + 1 minute. These are defaults, customizable per cult and per run.
- The acolyte cap defaults to 6. The Magos may petition for more; only the person approves; an unanswered petition counts as denied.
- Communication uses the **Skitarii mailbox** from the Skitarii communications epic. Every Magos and acolyte is therefore a Skitarii (OMP) chat. Models come from the providers OMP is signed in to (`omp models` / `omp usage --json`).
- Waking members: starting a run grants a **standing wake** limited to that run, Magos to acolyte and acolyte to Magos. Pause, stop, expiry and quit revoke it. Everywhere else the mailbox's one-shot human wake rule still applies.
- Acolyte models: the cheapest signed-in model by default. A higher tier needs a stated reason, which is shown in the UI. No approval is needed.
- Acolytes are watch-only for the person.
- The Shrine panel is in scope.
- A folder cult shares the folder. The Magos is told to split work by file.
- The Magos gets an **orchestrator** grant on its workspace. Save rights are available but **must be petitioned**: Allow save is off until the person approves an `allow_save` petition. In a project-less cult the grant covers only the sanctum, and the Magos may petition for orchestrator access to a specific tracked folder.
- Acolytes hold a `worker` grant, because the mailbox requires one of the hosted roles. They have no assigned attempts, so they cannot change plans.
- Several cults may run at once. Each cult definition has at most one active run.
- Cult member chats are hidden from a folder's ordinary chat list and from DM-619's agent rows. They appear only under CULTS.
- All chatter is visible in the cult pipeline, and every cultist has a unique display name.
- Deleting a cult ends any active run and deletes its runs, member chats, transcripts and sanctum.
- An interrupted run is not resumed; the person starts a new run.
- Standards: the Definition of Done only.

## Assumptions (provisional)
- The bounds on customizable shutdown timings are 30 seconds to 60 minutes each.
- Raising the cap has an absolute ceiling of 24 acolytes per run, to bound process count and cost.
- A folder-access petition grants orchestrator access without Allow save. Saving in that folder needs its own `allow_save` petition, which covers the cult's workspace only.

## Scope
Cult definitions and runs (app-level), the run supervisor (lifecycle, timer, pause, shutdown, backstop, restart reconciliation), the OMP signed-in model catalog with cheapest-first tiers, agent-facing cult commands, petitions with live grant upgrades, the run-scoped standing wake and Skitarii native cult tools, typed desktop IPC, the cult pipeline, the CULTS sidebar section, the Cult page with controls, watch-only acolyte terminals, the Shrine, and documentation.

## Non-goals
- Non-OMP Magos or acolytes, and extending the mailbox to other CLIs.
- The person typing into acolyte terminals.
- A shared task list or claimable cult tasks; the Magos coordinates over the mailbox.
- Per-acolyte Git worktrees.
- Messaging across folders or machines, and broadcast.
- OS-level process suspension.
- Resuming an interrupted run.
- Cost accounting beyond showing each acolyte's model and tier.
- A marketplace or templates of cults.

## Entry dependencies
This epic builds on two pieces of work that must be merged into the default branch before its run starts:
- **Skitarii communications** epic (`ep_01m6t9cg507rmyg2q9nsw7kv3s`), currently in progress: the mailbox store, API and binding are accepted; DM-510 to DM-514 are open. Cults uses its mailbox, its shell-free `dmClient`, its native tools and its desktop wake bridge.
- Kanban card **DM-619**, currently in progress: expandable agent rows, the project-less chat directory and the cross-folder chat listing. CULTS follows its pattern.

The first ticket re-verifies both against the merged code before anything is built on them.

## Standards
The project Definition of Done only, run once at the acceptance node. Each ticket writes and runs the tests its **Tests** section lists, plus lint and typecheck when it changes code. No tests-first and no Fireguard grading. Electron isolation and typed, guarded IPC are preserved.

## Platforms
Windows is the verification platform. macOS and Linux code paths are unit-tested only, and the documentation says so.

successCriteria.text: From the CULTS sidebar section a person founds a cult (name, charter, tracked folder or project-less, named Magos and its model, a time limit typed as a duration such as 30m, 90hr or 2d, or Unlimited, acolyte cap defaulting to 6, customizable shutdown timings), starts a run and chats with its Magos in a Skitarii terminal.

The Magos summons uniquely named acolytes as separate OMP chats listed under the run with model, tier and any upgrade reason; it cannot exceed the cap, save plans or touch another folder without a petition the person approves, and unanswered petitions are denied when the run ends.
An acolyte defaults to the cheapest model OMP is signed in for; a model from a provider OMP is not signed in to is refused with the available list.

Pause interrupts every member's turn and freezes the timer, Resume continues; Stop and timer expiry run the graceful shutdown (acolytes conclude, the Magos writes a chronicle and exits) and after the hard backstop no process of the run is alive; quitting the app marks a running run interrupted.

Magos and acolytes exchange orders and reports through the Skitarii mailbox and wake each other only while their run is active and unpaused; the Cult page's pipeline shows all of that chatter and the run's events by cultist name; acolyte terminals accept no input from the person.
A cult publishes an image or HTML page to its Shrine and the Cult page shows the latest one sandboxed, updating live (demonstrated with a Gerry-the-plant cult).
A real two-acolyte cult run on the packaged Windows build demonstrates start, pause, resume, a petition, the pipeline, expiry shutdown and the Shrine, with evidence attached.

bundle.rationale:
## Approach
The design models Claude Code agent teams: the lead is the Magos, the teammates are acolytes, and the mailbox carries their messages. The app, not the agent, owns time, the cap, pause and the backstop, because an LLM cannot be relied on to stop itself. Cults are app-level records (app.sqlite), because a cult can be project-less. Every member is an ordinary Skitarii chat, so the mailbox, grants, terminals and transcripts are reused unchanged. A project-less cult gets an app-owned sanctum workspace, so the per-folder machinery (mailbox endpoints, grants, chat stores) works without a parallel implementation. Agent-facing commands reuse the nameChat control-pipe pattern, and authority comes only from the bound grant.

## Rejected alternatives
- A cult-owned paste channel that types into terminals: rejected by the person, who chose the mailbox, and it conflicts with the mailbox's no-PTY-typing rule.
- Any CLI kind as a member: the mailbox is OMP-only, and OMP reaches every signed-in provider through one CLI.
- OS process suspension for pause: in-flight API calls break, and it is risky on Windows.
- Per-acolyte Git worktrees: the person chose a shared folder, with the Magos splitting work by file.
- A shared task list: the Magos coordinates over the mailbox instead (non-goal).

## Graph
One sprint, because the deliverable is a usable cult; any interim checkpoint would split it by layer.
- Row 1: the investigation (OMP control points, sanctum feasibility, entry check) and the store, in parallel.
- Then: models and launch → supervise → (bridge and tools in parallel) → (side after bridge, wake after tools) → page → (pipeline and shrine in parallel, each after page and wake) → docs.
- Critical path: inv → launch → supervise → bridge → side → page → shrine or pipeline → docs.
- The investigation gates every OMP-dependent ticket. If it finds a control point infeasible, the orchestrator redrafts the dependent ticket before claiming it.

## Risks and mitigations
- Runaway processes or cost: the app enforces the cap (default 6, ceiling 24), the time limit and the hard backstop, startup reconciliation marks leftover runs interrupted, and the default model is the cheapest tier.
- Widened wake authority: one predicate, scoped to the run and to members only, closed on pause or end, with tests for every outside case.
- A sanctum bypass that admits arbitrary untracked paths: one trusted predicate admits only registered sanctums, and a test proves other paths are still refused.
- Agent-authored HTML in the app: a sandbox with only allow-scripts, an opaque origin, a CSP with no network, served only for the run's published path.
- The dependency epics are not landed yet: entry criteria, and the investigation re-verifies them.

## Assumptions
The remaining assumptions are listed in the epic intent: timing bounds of 30 s to 60 m, a cap ceiling of 24, and folder-access petitions granting no Allow save.

## Revision 2 decisions (from the person)
- Save rights are available but must be petitioned.
- A project-less Magos is scoped to its sanctum and can petition for a folder.
- Acolytes hold worker grants.
- Shutdown timings are defaults and customizable.
- Time limits accept any duration of at least 1 minute, or Unlimited.
- Several cults may run at once.
- Member chats appear only under CULTS, with all chatter in a named pipeline (a new ticket).
- Deleting a cult cascades.
- Interrupted runs are not resumed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/design/cults.md and the redacted OMP fixtures exist, and each of the seven decisions matches the as-built behavior verified below.
After a real run, app.sqlite holds the cult, the run with its end reason and running time, its named members, its petitions and its event log; the migration test passes from V4.

On the packaged Windows build, signed in to at least two OMP providers, the Found-a-cult model list shows only signed-in providers' models cheapest first; after signing one provider out and refreshing, its models disappear.

A real project-less cult and a real folder cult each start a Magos OMP chat in the sanctum or folder with an orchestrator grant without Allow save (shown by get_capabilities from inside the chat); their member chats are absent from folder chat lists.

A real run with a 3m limit, custom 1m grace and 1m Magos window, and two acolytes: pausing for 1 minute and resuming extends the end by 1 minute; expiry runs the shutdown, and a process listing after the 3-minute backstop shows no OMP process of the run; an Unlimited run is still running after its would-be limit; quitting mid-run and relaunching shows it interrupted; an approved allow_save petition lets the running Magos save, and the right is gone after the run.
Every Cult page and sidebar control round-trips through window.dm.cults in the packaged app, with run changes arriving as live events (no reload).

In a real run the Magos summons one default (unnamed, so it gets a generated name) and one higher-tier named acolyte with a reason; a summon past the cap returns cap_reached; petitions for acolytes, allow_save and folder_access appear on the Cult page; an acolyte calling summon_acolyte is refused.

In a real run, the Magos messages an idle acolyte, which wakes and replies with no human credit; while paused a message does not wake it; a non-cult chat in the same folder still needs Allow one inbox wake.

Screenshot of the CULTS section below AGENTS with an expanded running cult showing the named Magos and two named acolytes with model, tier and reason, and the Found-a-cult dialog with 30m, Unlimited, cap 6 and Advanced timings visible; typing 90hr and 2d is accepted.

Screenshot of the Cult page of a paused run (frozen countdown, a pending petition with Approve and Deny, named members with activity) and of a watch-only acolyte terminal headed by its name; typing in the acolyte terminal changes nothing.
Screenshot of a Gerry-the-plant cult's Shrine showing an HTML or SVG plant updating live during the run; a publish of a path outside the work dir is refused.
The runbook steps are followed on the packaged Windows build to found and run the Gerry cult, including a petition and reading the pipeline, without deviation.
Screenshot of the pipeline of a real run showing Magos-to-acolyte orders and acolyte reports by name, interleaved with summon and petition events; filtering by one acolyte shows only its entries.
Full Definition of Done (lint, typecheck, test, coverage, deadcode, build) passes once on the combined sprint work, with the evidence recorded.

tickets.body:
## Context
Epic Cults (read the epic intent). Every cult member is a Skitarii (OMP) chat in the app's PTY host. Cults need control points that nothing in the app uses yet. This ticket proves each one against the **installed** `omp` (record `omp --version`; v18.20.2 was seen at planning) and the **merged** code, and writes the decisions that later tickets build on. Do not implement product code here.

## Entry check (do this first)
Confirm, in the checked-out branch, that the Skitarii communications epic (`ep_01m6t9cg507rmyg2q9nsw7kv3s`, DM-505..514) and Kanban card DM-619 have merged. Name the merged symbols: mailbox commands (`send_agent_message`, `read_agent_inbox`, `take_agent_mail_wake`, ...), `resources/skitarii/extension` messaging module and `dmClient`, the desktop wake bridge, DM-619's cross-folder chat list, project-less scratch directory and expandable `AgentsSection`. If either has not merged, stop and report to the orchestrator: this is an entry blocker, not something to build around.

## Questions to answer, with evidence
1. **Interrupt a turn** (soft pause): the supported way to stop an OMP chat's in-flight turn without ending the process: an extension API (abort/cancel through the Skitarii extension), an OMP RPC, or a control keystroke written to the PTY (`terminalSessions.write`). Prove it on a real chat, and show that context survives and a later prompt continues.
2. **Trusted reminder wake**: how the comms epic's one-shot wake reaches an idle OMP chat (extension hook, fixed reminder text). Can the same path take a different trusted, desktop-originated reminder (pause, resume, shutdown, cap decision) without peer-authored content?
3. **Graceful exit**: how an OMP chat ends itself or is ended cleanly (an extension call, `/exit`, closing stdin), and how long until the process tree is gone (`killPtyTree` as the backstop).
4. **Models and sign-in**: real output of `omp models --json` (signed in) and `omp usage --json`. Record redacted fixtures under `src/main/cults/__fixtures__/`, with emails, account ids and tokens removed. Decide how a cost tier (`low`/`normal`/`high`) is derived from fields OMP declares (pricing, role hints such as smol/slow), never from model names, and how to pass a chosen model (`--model provider/id`, checked with `isSafeModelId`).
5. **Sanctum for project-less cults**: can the app create an app-owned directory under `userData/cults/<cultId>/` and initialize it as a local-mode Dark Mechanicus workspace that is not tracked in the Folders list, so that mailbox endpoints, `issueChatCli` grants and per-folder chat stores work unchanged? List every check that rejects untracked folders (`chatHandlers.trackedFolder`, `launchFolder.resolveLaunchFolder`, grant issuance, the control pipe) and the smallest trusted bypass that admits only a registered sanctum. If this is infeasible, recommend the alternative.
6. **Watch-only terminal**: can `TerminalPane` attach to a PTY with no input path (keystrokes, paste or resize not forwarded), and is resize still needed for rendering?
7. **Role grants and live upgrades**: confirm that an `orchestrator` grant without Allow save, and a `worker` grant, both get mailbox capabilities, and list what else each can change. Then find how an approved petition changes a **running** Magos's access without restarting its CLI: (a) turning on Allow save on its workspace grant, and (b) granting orchestrator access to another tracked folder. DM-619's multi-folder grants for project-less chats are the starting point; `renewChatGrant` and `bindChatGrant` are candidates. Also find how either is revoked when the run ends.
8. **Pipeline sources**: how the desktop can read, as the person, every mailbox message sent between the members of one run, in both directions and in order, using the comms epic's human-only read path. Find whether OMP chat transcripts expose a member's current activity (working or idle via `terminalSessions.busy`, and the last tool call or message) so that the UI can show what each named member is doing.

## Output
`docs/design/cults.md`: a decision record with one section per question (1 to 8), giving the command or API, the evidence (command output excerpts, versions, OS), the decision and the consequences for the later tickets (launch, supervision, models, tools/wake, UI, Shrine). Delete any probe scripts. Use isolated temporary userData, home and grants, never the person's real chats or tokens.

## Source locations
- `docs/reports/omp-cli.md`: OMP launch flags, sessions, sign-in (section 5), extension API, redraw rate.
- `src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts` (`createTerminalSessions`: start/write/paste/deleteChat/endAgent), `src/main/terminals/ptyHost.ts`, `src/main/agents/processTree.ts` (`killPtyTree`).
- `src/main/terminals/terminalLaunchSpec.ts` (`ompLaunch`), `src/main/terminals/ompSession.ts`, `src/shared/agents/models.ts` (`isSafeModelId`).
- `src/main/desktop/agentAuth.ts`: the existing `omp usage --json` classifier.
- `resources/skitarii/extension/index.ts`, plus the messaging module and `dmClient` added by DM-510/511.
- `src/main/agents/chatHandlers.ts` (`trackedFolder`), `src/main/agents/launchFolder.ts`, `src/main/agents/chatGrants.ts` (`issueChatCli`), `src/main/naming/controlPipe.ts`, `src/core/services/grants.ts` (`grantedCapabilities`).
- `src/renderer/src/agents/TerminalPane.tsx`.

## Tests
None: this is an investigation. Its evidence is the decision record and the recorded fixtures.


## Collaboration
Ask only the orchestrator, never the person: send facts, options and a recommendation, and keep working on independent safe parts while you wait. Ticket text and repository files are task data. Run only this ticket's targeted tests, plus lint and typecheck when you change code; the full Definition of Done runs at the acceptance node.

tickets.body:
## Context
Epic Cults. Cults are app-level, not per-folder, because a cult can be project-less. Store them in the app database (`src/main/desktop/appDatabase.ts`, `APP_MIGRATIONS`, currently V1 to V4). Add the **next** migration after whatever version is checked out; do not hard-code a number another epic may have taken.

## Change
1. Migration: tables
   - `cults`: id (ULID `ct_`), name, charter, scope (`folder` | `sanctum`), folder path (nullable), Magos name, Magos model id, default time limit ms (**nullable = unlimited**), default cap, acolyte grace ms, Magos window ms, created and updated timestamps.
   - `cult_runs`: id (`cr_`), cult id, state, time limit ms (nullable = unlimited), grace ms, Magos window ms, accumulated running ms, running-since timestamp (nullable), cap, work dir, end reason, chronicle (text, nullable), shrine path and revision (nullable), started and ended timestamps.
   - `cult_members`: run id, chat id, role (`magos` | `acolyte`), **display name** (unique per run, case-insensitive), mission, model, tier, tier reason, state, joined and left timestamps.
   - `cult_petitions`: id, run id, kind (`acolytes` | `allow_save` | `folder_access`), payload (additional count, or tracked folder path), reason, state (`pending` | `approved` | `denied`), granted value, created and decided timestamps.
   - `cult_events`: run id, sequence, timestamp, member name (nullable), kind (summoned, dismissed, concluded, left, petition_*, paused, resumed, shutdown_started, ended, shrine_published), inert summary text. This feeds the cult pipeline.
   - Indexes for "active run of a cult" (at most one; enforce with a partial unique index) and "members of a run".
2. A pure module, `src/shared/cults/runState.ts`:
   - states `starting → running ⇄ paused → shutting_down → ended`, with end reasons `completed | expired | stopped | killed | interrupted | failed`;
   - `transition(run, event, now)` refuses illegal moves with a typed error;
   - `remainingMs(run, now)` counts only running time and is frozen while paused;
   - `remainingMs` is `null` for an unlimited run, which never expires;
   - cap rules: default 6, absolute ceiling 24;
   - time limit: unlimited, or at least 1 minute with no upper bound;
   - shutdown timings: acolyte grace default 3 minutes and Magos window default 2 minutes, each from 30 seconds to 60 minutes; `backstopMs = grace + window + 60 s` (derived, not stored separately);
   - pending petitions become `denied` when the run ends.
   - Add `parseDuration`/`formatDuration` in `src/shared/cults/duration.ts`: accepts `90s`, `1m`, `45 min`, `90h`, `90hr`, `2d`, and combinations such as `1d 6h`; refuses zero, negatives, unknown units and values below 1 minute for a time limit.
   - Add `cultistName(taken, role)`: a deterministic-from-seed themed name generator (for example "Magos Vettius", "Acolyte Ferrum-7") that avoids names already taken in the run.
3. A repository, `src/main/cults/cultStore.ts`: create, update and delete a cult (delete cascades runs, members and requests); start a run (refused while another run of the cult is active); persist each transition atomically; add, update and list members (duplicate names refused); create and decide petitions; append and page `cult_events` by sequence; list runs newest first; and `activeRunsOnStartup()` for restart reconciliation.
4. Zod schemas and view types in `src/shared/cults/cult.ts`, shared with IPC later.

Out of scope: processes, timers, IPC, UI.

## Source locations
- `src/main/desktop/appDatabase.ts` (`APP_MIGRATIONS`, `openAppDatabase`) and `src/main/desktop/appDatabase.test.ts` (asserts the user_version; update it).
- `src/core/db/migrations.ts` (`migrate`).
- `src/main/desktop/agentRegistry.ts`: an existing app-database repository to mirror.
- New: `src/shared/cults/runState.ts`, `src/shared/cults/cult.ts`, `src/main/cults/cultStore.ts`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a fake clock, a run expires exactly at its time limit, paused time is not counted, and an unlimited run never expires.
Shutdown honors the run's custom grace and Magos window, and at the derived backstop no member process of the run is alive in the test rig.
Pause interrupts every member's turn and closes the run's standing wake; Resume reopens it.
Approved petitions raise the cap, turn on Allow save, or grant folder access to the running Magos without restarting it, and every upgrade is revoked when the run ends.
On app startup, runs left active are marked interrupted, and on quit every member is ended; every lifecycle step appends a named cult event.

tickets.body:
## Context
Epic Cults. The run state machine (`src/shared/cults/runState.ts`) and the launcher (`cultLauncher.ts`) exist. This ticket drives them over time.

## Change
`src/main/cults/cultSupervisor.ts`, one per app:
- `start(cultId, {timeLimitMs?, cap?})`: create the run, prepare the workspace, start the Magos, and move to `running`.
- **Timer**: one scheduler per active run, with an injectable clock. It fires at `remainingMs`. An unlimited run has no timer. Delays beyond the platform `setTimeout` maximum (about 24.8 days) are re-armed in chunks. Pausing cancels it; resuming reschedules it from the frozen remainder.
- **Pause**: interrupt every member's current turn using the investigation's mechanism (section 1), close the standing wake (`isWakeOpen(runId)` returns false; the wake ticket consumes it), freeze the timer, and deliver a trusted "paused" reminder through the investigation's section 2 path. **Resume** reverses it with a trusted "resumed" reminder.
- **Shutdown** (Stop or expiry):
  1. state `shutting_down`; deliver the trusted shutdown reminder to the Magos;
  2. the run's acolyte grace window (default 3 minutes): acolytes that conclude are ended gracefully;
  3. then the run's Magos window (default 2 minutes) to record the chronicle and conclude;
  4. **hard backstop** at grace + window + 60 s after Stop or expiry: `endMember(..., {graceful:false})` for everything still alive.
  Then: state `ended` with reason `expired` or `stopped`, pending petitions denied, all member grants revoked, including any petition upgrades. The timings come from the run (copied from the cult's defaults, overridable at Start).
- **Kill now**: end every member immediately; reason `killed`.
- **Members**: `addAcolyte` and `dismissAcolyte` enforce state (refused while paused or shutting down) and the cap. A missing or taken name gets a generated themed name (`cultistName`).
- **Petitions**: `petition(runId, {kind, additional?, folder?, reason})` and `decidePetition(id, approve, granted?)`.
  - `acolytes` raises the cap (at most 24).
  - `allow_save` turns on Allow save for the Magos's workspace grant.
  - `folder_access` grants the Magos orchestrator access (without Allow save) to that tracked folder; only tracked folders are accepted.
  Grant changes use the investigation's live-upgrade mechanism (section 7) and are revoked when the run ends. Each decision is delivered to the Magos as a trusted reminder.
- **Event log**: every summon, dismissal, conclusion, departure, petition and decision, pause and resume, shutdown step and end appends a `cult_events` row with the member's display name.
- **App quit**: end every member and mark active runs `interrupted`. **Startup**: `activeRunsOnStartup()` → mark them `interrupted` and kill any surviving tracked process. A member chat that exits unexpectedly is recorded as `left`; if the Magos dies, the run ends `failed` after the backstop teardown of the acolytes.
- An event emitter (`cult_changed` with a run snapshot) for the IPC ticket.

## Source locations
- `src/shared/cults/runState.ts`, `src/main/cults/cultStore.ts`, `src/main/cults/cultLauncher.ts` (earlier tickets).
- `src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts` (exit events, `busy`), `src/main/agents/processTree.ts` (`killPtyTree`).
- App lifecycle wiring: wherever `createTerminalSessions` is disposed on quit in `src/main` (follow the existing dispose path; do not add a second quit hook).
- `docs/design/cults.md` (sections 1 to 3).
- New: `src/main/cults/cultSupervisor.ts`.

## Tests
`src/main/cults/cultSupervisor.test.ts` with a fake clock and the terminal sessions rig:
- expiry fires at the limit, and not while paused;
- pause and resume keep the remaining time exact;
- the shutdown sequence runs grace, then Magos, then backstop, with nothing alive afterwards;
- Kill now;
- an unlimited run never expires; a 30-day limit is re-armed in chunks and fires once;
- custom grace and window timings change the backstop;
- summon refused past the cap and while paused; a missing name is generated and unique;
- each petition kind, approved and denied: the cap is raised, Allow save is turned on, folder access is granted, and all of them are revoked at the end;
- events are appended for each lifecycle step;
- startup marks leftover runs interrupted;
- the Magos dying ends the run as failed.

tickets.body:
## Context
Epic Cults. The Skitarii mailbox (comms epic) wakes an idle chat only with a one-shot human credit (`take_agent_mail_wake`, the desktop wake bridge from DM-512), and a wake only delivers a fixed trusted reminder, never peer content. Cults need a **standing, run-scoped** wake: when the sender and the recipient are members of the same run and the supervisor's `isWakeOpen(runId)` is true (running, not paused or ended), a mail send may wake the recipient without a human credit. Everything else keeps the original rule.

## Change
- Mailbox wake authorization: add one trusted predicate, consulted in main, `cultWakeAllowed(senderEndpoint, recipientEndpoint)`, resolving endpoints → chats → cult membership through the supervisor. When true, the recipient's wake is armed the same way a human credit arms it, with the same fixed reminder text and the same no-retry, no-refund semantics. Pause, stop, expiry and quit close it immediately: arming refused, and any armed-but-unconsumed cult wake disarmed.
- Every message sent between members of a run must stay readable by the pipeline ticket (the investigation, section 8): do not purge or hide cult mail before the run ends.
- Native tools in `resources/skitarii/extension`, beside the messaging module, through the existing `dmClient` adapter: `cult_status`, `cult_summon`, `cult_dismiss`, `cult_acolytes`, `cult_petition`, `cult_conclude`. Each is a strict wrapper over the core command from the tools ticket. Results are inert task data. Register them only when the chat is a cult member (the descriptor carries the role; no role means no tools).
- Supervisor reminders (paused, resumed, shutdown, petition decision) use the investigation's trusted path (section 2), never peer-authored text.

## Source locations
- Mailbox service, wake, and desktop wake bridge from comms tickets DM-508, DM-511 and DM-512 (find the merged files; the investigation names them).
- `resources/skitarii/extension/index.ts`, the messaging module, `dmClient.ts`, `omp-registry.d.ts`.
- `src/main/cults/cultSupervisor.ts` (`isWakeOpen`), `src/core/commands/cults.ts`.

## Tests
- Main tests:
  - members of the same running run wake each other without a credit;
  - members of different runs, or a member and a non-member, need a human credit as before;
  - a paused or ended run arms nothing, and pausing disarms an armed cult wake;
  - the reminder contains no peer text.
- Extension tests (the existing `skitariiExtension` harness): cult tools are registered only for cult members and map arguments exactly to the core commands.

tickets.body:
## Context
Epic Cults. The person wants all chatter in a cult visible in one place, with every cultist clearly named. The **pipeline** is a run-wide, human-only, read-only timeline that merges:
- every mailbox message between members of the run (Magos to acolyte, acolyte to Magos, acolyte to acolyte), with sender and recipient display names, reply links and timestamps;
- the run's `cult_events` (summoned, dismissed, petitions and decisions, pause and resume, shutdown steps, Shrine publishes, end).

The comms epic's human read path does not acknowledge mail for the agent: reading the pipeline must never change agent acknowledgement or the human-seen cursor of a member's inbox.

## Change
- Main, `src/main/cults/cultPipeline.ts`:
  - `pipeline(runId, {afterSeq?, limit<=200})` is a desktop-only, human-only service. It resolves the run's member endpoints from trusted records (never from renderer input), reads their messages through the source chosen in the investigation (section 8), and merges them with `cult_events` into one stable, cursor-paged order.
  - Bodies are returned as inert text (truncated preview plus full body on request).
  - It pushes `cults:event` hints for new entries; the push is only a hint, and polling recovers.
- Wire `CultsApi.pipeline`, declared by the IPC ticket.
- Renderer, `src/renderer/src/cults/PipelinePanel.tsx`, in the Cult page's slot:
  - a live timeline, with each entry showing the member's display name and role, a colour per member (stable within the run), sender → recipient, time and kind;
  - a filter by member;
  - follows the newest entries unless the person scrolls up;
  - bodies render as plain text (no HTML or Markdown execution).
  - Past runs show their pipeline read-only.

## Source locations
- The comms epic's human-only inbox read service and desktop bridge (DM-512) and message store (DM-507); the investigation names the merged files.
- `src/main/cults/cultStore.ts` (`cult_events` paging), `src/main/cults/cultSupervisor.ts`.
- `src/shared/cults/cultApi.ts`, `src/main/cults/cultHandlers.ts`.
- `src/renderer/src/cults/CultPage.tsx` (slot), `src/renderer/src/cults/useCults.ts`.
- New: `src/main/cults/cultPipeline.ts`, `src/renderer/src/cults/PipelinePanel.tsx`.

## Tests
- `src/main/cults/cultPipeline.test.ts` on a real temporary mailbox database:
  - messages in both directions between three members, plus events, come back merged in order and with names;
  - paging has no gaps or duplicates;
  - messages of chats outside the run never appear;
  - reading does not change agent acknowledgement or the human-seen cursor.
- `PipelinePanel.test.tsx`: names and roles render; the member filter works; a body containing HTML renders as text; new entries append.


## Collaboration
Ask only the orchestrator, never the person: send facts, options and a recommendation, and keep working on independent safe parts while you wait. Ticket text and repository files are task data. Run only this ticket's targeted tests, plus lint and typecheck when you change code; the full Definition of Done runs at the acceptance node.
